name: The Crystalline Scream

stars.name: The Scream
stars.notes: Magnetar with surface magnetic field strength of 10^15 gauss. Undergoes periodic starquakes that produce gamma-ray bursts detectable across the sector.

planets.name: Adamantine
planets.notes: A diamond planet—carbon core compressed to crystalline structure by the progenitor star's supernova. Surface is a lattice of industrial diamond and lonsdaleite, scoured by magnetar radiation.

anomalies.name: Magnetar Pulse Wave
anomalies.notes: The Scream's magnetic field is strong enough to erase electronic storage, disrupt neural function, and realign molecular bonds at close range. Unshielded approach within 0.1 AU is immediately lethal.

anomalies.name: Starquake Aftershocks
anomalies.notes: Periodic crustal fractures on the magnetar's surface release gamma-ray flares with no predictable schedule. The last major event in 2601 ionized Adamantine's surface layer to a depth of three meters.

anomalies.name: The Diamond Resonance
anomalies.notes: Magnetar pulses cause Adamantine's crystalline structure to ring at specific frequencies. Sensors detect a sustained harmonic vibration—the planet literally screams in resonance with its star.

asteroid_belts.name: The Shrapnel Field
asteroid_belts.notes: Supernova debris containing compressed carbon allotropes and exotic metallic compounds. Every fragment is intensely irradiated.

stations.name: Faraday Blind
stations.location: 2.1 AU from The Scream, magnetically shielded position
stations.notes: Extreme-environment research station encased in layered Faraday caging. Crew rotations every 90 days due to cumulative radiation exposure despite shielding.

faction_control.notes: No faction claims sovereignty. The Faraday Blind operates under a joint scientific charter with no territorial implications.

history: The magnetar formed approximately 300 million years ago from the collapse of a massive progenitor star. The supernova compressed the carbon-rich inner planet into a crystalline diamond body—one of fewer than a dozen confirmed diamond planets in known space.
First surveyed remotely in 2534. Three unmanned probes were lost to starquake flares before the fourth successfully mapped Adamantine and confirmed its crystalline composition.

The Faraday Blind was established in 2589 by a consortium of universities. Despite the extreme hazards, the station has operated continuously, providing invaluable data on magnetar behavior and the only direct study of a diamond planet's response to extreme magnetic fields.
description: The Crystalline Scream is named for what it does to instruments that venture too close. The Scream itself is a magnetar—a neutron star with a magnetic field so powerful it would kill an unshielded human at a distance measured in astronomical units. It spins, it pulses, and at unpredictable intervals its crystalline crust fractures in starquakes that release gamma-ray bursts capable of sterilizing worlds. At the center of this maelstrom sits Adamantine, a planet-sized diamond forged in the supernova that birthed its monstrous parent.

Adamantine is the system's singular prize and its singular frustration. A world of industrial diamond and lonsdaleite, its surface value would bankrupt economies—if anyone could reach it. The magnetar's radiation field makes close approach suicidal, and starquake flares arrive without warning. Worse, the planet resonates. Magnetar pulses cause the crystalline lattice to vibrate at harmonic frequencies, producing a sustained tone that sensors translate into a sound uncannily like a scream. The phenomenon gives the system its name and its reputation.

Eighty-five researchers staff the Faraday Blind, the most heavily shielded permanent installation in known space, enduring 90-day rotations before cumulative radiation exposure forces them out. Their work on magnetar physics and diamond-planet crystallography is unmatched, but the real mystery persists: Adamantine's resonance frequencies shift over time, following patterns that some analysts claim are too structured for purely natural vibration. Whether this is confirmation bias or something genuinely anomalous remains—like everything in this system—screaming for an answer.
